A compact weekly note for maintainers.

Systems Letter No. 27

Evidence has a lifetime

A reconciler depends on terminal queue rows as evidence. Retention can be finite, but only when its configured lifetime exceeds every supported detection and recovery delay.

Read only what you use

A narrow database projection is valuable when it reduces transfer and scan work or when its interface removes facts a caller does not need. Measure both claims with fixed light and heavy rows.

One practical question

Can a new caller add a field to a projection without naming the behavior that consumes it? A field-to-consumer guard turns that design question into a reviewable test.
